# Review a cross-border personal data transfer

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before allowing a new international data flow or materially changing a receiving supplier. A documented transfer decision with applicable safeguards, contracts and technical controls verified.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Map the actual transfer and access paths

agent-runnable


Identify the exporter, importer, data, purpose, storage locations and remote-access locations. Include onward transfers and supplier support access rather than relying only on the cloud region label.

- Sources: [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Determine the applicable transfer requirements

human · human approval required


Qualified privacy advisers assess the relevant jurisdictions, roles and available transfer mechanisms. Record the basis and conditions for the specific flow, including unresolved local-law or supplier questions.

- Sources: [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the contract and risk evidence

agent-runnable


Assemble the proposed terms, supplier disclosures, security measures and any required assessment. Describe technical controls and alternatives without assuming a signed template alone resolves the risks.

- Sources: [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve and implement the defined transfer

human · human approval required


Authorized owners execute reviewed agreements and configure the approved access and security measures. Keep unapproved destinations and onward transfers blocked and retain the decision evidence.

- Sources: [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Monitor supplier and legal changes

agent-runnable


Review changes in subprocessors, locations, purposes or safeguards and track contract obligations. Reassess the transfer when its documented assumptions change and suspend flows where required conditions are no longer met.

- Verify: A documented transfer decision with applicable safeguards, contracts and technical controls verified.
- Sources: [European Commission international data protection](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection_en) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)
